channel_type: 14-track one-inch instrumentation magnetic tape (SSTV + mission telemetry)
discard_mechanism: degaussed and recertified for reuse by NASA/Goddard in early 1980s tape scarcity
inference_statement: INFERENCE: the raw SSTV signal held higher-resolution signal information than the converted broadcast; that higher-quality information is unrecoverable. NOT claimed: unseen scenes or suppressed footage — NASA says no unseen moonwalk video was lost, and the record is treated as authoritative on that point.
known_fact: A 2009 NASA search concluded ~45 raw slow-scan telemetry tapes were likely degaussed and reused circa 1981-82 to support Landsat and the shuttle program. The live-converted NTSC broadcast survives in many archives; the raw higher-quality SSTV channel does not. NASA emphasized no unseen moonwalk video was lost.
name: Apollo 11 raw slow-scan telemetry tapes degaussed and reused
notes: Primary DCC instance. Procedural erasure of a channel that existed, not undersampling. The lost remainder is signal quality / future reprocessing capacity, not unknown scenes.

channel_type: analog master recording tapes and multitrack session reels (UMG vault)
discard_mechanism: accidental fire, June 1 2008; archive had been downplayed as a 'video vault' of copies
inference_statement: INFERENCE: unreleased sessions and isolated-instrument multitracks that were never cataloged publicly are gone and can never be enumerated from the surviving commercial catalog. NOT claimed: specific unreleased tracks exist — only that the vault inventory, per the NYT investigation, included never-released sessions whose contents no surviving record enumerates.
known_fact: NYT Magazine investigation (June 2019, Jody Rosen): more than 175,000 master tapes destroyed, estimated ~500,000 song titles. Almost all Buddy Holly masters; most of John Coltrane's Impulse catalog; all Decca masters (Holiday, Armstrong, Ellington, Fitzgerald, Berry); multitracks; sessions never released. UMG had told Billboard in 2008 it 'had no loss.'
name: 2008 Universal backlot fire destroyed ~175,000 master recording tapes
notes: Cited source is Metal Insider's account of the NYT Magazine investigation (paywalled at NYT). Corroborated by the class-action complaint filing against UMG (digitalmusicnews PDF, 2019). Commercial releases survive; the master-quality channel and unreleased-session remainder do not.

channel_type: cellulose-nitrate theatrical film elements (1912-1929 features)
discard_mechanism: decay, studio fires, deliberate destruction/melting for silver content, neglect
inference_statement: INFERENCE: the lost 70% contained creative works no surviving catalog enumerates; each lost title is an unenumerated remainder. Source establishes the scale of loss, not any specific film's contents.
known_fact: LoC's first comprehensive survey of 10,919 American silent features: ~70% believed lost; only 14% (1,575 titles) survive in original 35mm; 11% survive only as foreign versions or lower-quality formats. 'An alarming and irretrievable loss to our nation's cultural record' (Librarian of Congress James H. Billington).
name: 70% of American silent feature films lost (Library of Congress 2013)
notes: Aggregate-instance: DCC claims the class-level shape, not any single title. The LoC study is the primary institutional source.

channel_type: nitrate film vault archive (Fox Film Corporation + Educational Pictures negatives)
discard_mechanism: spontaneous combustion of decaying nitrate in heat wave, July 9 1937; no sprinklers or ventilation
inference_statement: INFERENCE: the destroyed vault contents included titles whose only records were the destroyed elements; the full contents of the vault were never enumerated before the fire.
known_fact: All archived film in the vaults destroyed; loss of most silent films produced by Fox Film Corporation before 1932, plus negatives from Educational Pictures and other studios. 1 death, 2 injuries.
name: 1937 Fox vault fire, Little Ferry NJ — most Fox silent films pre-1932 destroyed
notes: Wikipedia is secondary; the event is corroborated across film-preservation literature. Theda Bara's near-total filmography loss is commonly cited from this fire.

channel_type: nitrate film vault archive (MGM + predecessors Metro/Goldwyn/Louis B. Mayer Pictures)
discard_mechanism: electrical short ignited stored nitrate, August 10 1965; entire vault contents destroyed
inference_statement: INFERENCE: 'only known copies' per the source means no surviving record can enumerate the destroyed reels' full contents; specific destroyed-only titles are known from secondary records, but their complete vault contents were not enumerated before the fire.
known_fact: The only known copies of hundreds of silent and early-sound films were destroyed, including London After Midnight (1927), The Divine Woman (1928), the last known print of The Rogue Song, and original-release prints of pre-1951 MGM cartoons including the silent Our Gang shorts 1927-1929.
name: 1965 MGM Vault 7 fire, Culver City — only known copies of hundreds of films destroyed
notes: Secondary source (Wikipedia); event corroborated in lost-film literature (e.g., collider.com lost-films history).

channel_type: handwritten manuscript census schedules (paper records channel)
discard_mechanism: fire in Commerce Department basement, January 10 1921 (25% burned, 50% water-damaged); Congress authorized disposal 1933; destroyed 1934-35
inference_statement: INFERENCE: the destroyed schedules held the only enumerations of millions of 1890 households; no other record enumerates what was on the destroyed pages. Source establishes the destruction, not any specific destroyed person's data.
known_fact: Only 6,160 persons listed in surviving population-census fragments (M407, 3 rolls, fragments in 10 states + DC). Veterans schedules, Oklahoma territorial schedules, and Delaware African-American lists partially survived. A 20-year genealogical gap 1880-1900 resulted.
name: 1890 US Census schedules destroyed in 1921 Commerce Department fire
notes: Primary institutional source (NARA). Note the two-stage discard: 1921 fire damage, then deliberate disposal authorized by Congress in 1933.

channel_type: Official Military Personnel Files (OMPFs), paper records channel
discard_mechanism: fire at 9700 Page Avenue, St. Louis, July 12 1973; burned 22+ hours out of control; water + mold damaged survivors; source never determined
inference_statement: INFERENCE: the destroyed files held service details not present in the alternate sources used for reconstruction; the reconstruction records themselves show the primary channel cannot be enumerated. Source establishes destruction scale and the reconstruction practice, not any specific destroyed file's contents.
known_fact: An estimated 16-18 million OMPFs of Army/Army Air Force/Air Force personnel discharged 1912-1964 damaged or destroyed; ~6.5 million survived in varying condition. 80% loss for Army 1912-1960; 75% for Air Force 1947-1964. NPRC reconstructs service from alternate sources (~5.5 million reconstructions).
name: 1973 National Personnel Records Center fire — 16-18 million military personnel files
notes: Primary source (NARA). 'Unparalleled disaster' per Archivist David S. Ferriero. Reconstruction from alternate sources proves G8: more records elsewhere cannot reconstruct the destroyed channel itself.

channel_type: 2-inch videotape broadcast masters
discard_mechanism: routine tape reuse/erasure per standard industry procedure; Carson discovered in 1972 that NBC held no archive
inference_statement: INFERENCE: the erased decade contained interviews and performances not documented in surviving records; the erased contents cannot be enumerated because the masters were the record. NOT claimed: any specific lost moment — the Dean Martin April 1973 anecdote is unverified YouTube lore and is NOT used as evidence.
known_fact: Only 33 episodes originally aired prior to May 1, 1972 are known to survive erasure by NBC, including Carson's debut (audio survives). The archive is virtually complete 1973-1992 after Carson took control of masters.
name: NBC wiped Johnny Carson Tonight Show master tapes, 1962-1972
notes: Some kinescopes survive via Armed Forces Radio and Television Service and guest collections (DVIDS, 1963 reel recovery). Secondary source; the DVIDS military-recovery story corroborates the erasure.

channel_type: kinescope film recordings of network broadcasts (1946-1956)
discard_mechanism: much destroyed ~1958 to recover silver content; remaining kinescopes reportedly dumped into Upper New York Bay in the 1970s after custody passed to successor companies
inference_statement: INFERENCE: the destroyed archive contained early-television programming whose contents no surviving record enumerates; early programs (Captain Video, Cavalcade of Stars) survive only in fragments. The dumping mechanism is partly unverified lore and is NOT presented as settled fact.
known_fact: Of 20,000+ episodes, ~350 survive, mostly in personal collections (Jackie Gleason preserved his own Honeymooners sketches). Edie Adams testified to the Library of Congress in 1996 about the alleged 1970s dumping; the bay-dumping account is commonly reported lore — the source notes 'no one really knows for sure what happened.'
name: DuMont Television Network archive destroyed — ~20,000 episodes to ~350 survivors
notes: Internet Archive blog is credible-secondary; it explicitly flags the bay-dumping as unverified lore. The silver-recovery destruction ~1958 is the firmer mechanism.

channel_type: 14-inch half-inch magnetic instrumentation tape reels (planetary probe telemetry)
discard_mechanism: IBM/NASA disposed of the reels circa 1968-1972; an IBM engineer took ~325 reels home; found mold-damaged in a Pittsburgh basement, recovered by NASA OIG December 2015
inference_statement: INFERENCE: most reels are unmarked, so their contents cannot be enumerated from any surviving inventory; whether the mold-damaged telemetry remains readable is unknown. NOT claimed: that the data is already lost — recovery status is unknown.
known_fact: NASA OIG report: 325 reels picked up Dec 8, 2015; most unmarked; majority appear to be Pioneer 10/11 instrumentation reels; 'poor condition and almost all affected by moderate to severe mould.' The engineer was told he could have them when IBM was getting rid of the items.
name: Pioneer 10/11 and Helios instrumentation reels abandoned, later found mold-damaged in engineer's basement
notes: Primary source (NASA OIG FOIA report). Lowest-certainty instance: the channel physically survives in degraded form, so DCC holds only for the unenumerated, possibly-unreadable remainder.

channel_type: broadcast videotape masters of television episodes
discard_mechanism: systematic junking policy: tape reuse, storage space, materials scarcity, rights constraints
inference_statement: INFERENCE: the missing broadcast-quality masters are the unenumerated remainder — surviving audio/stills enumerate content, not the visual channel as transmitted. Discrepant counts (95/97/106) are preserved, not resolved.
known_fact: Search result reported 95 of 253 early episodes missing; other tallies use 97 or 106 depending on date and counting method. Audio recordings, stills, and telesnaps survive for many episodes; some recovered from overseas broadcasters and private collections.
name: BBC wiped Doctor Who episodes 1967-1978
notes: Partial survival (audio, stills, some recovered episodes) weakens G5; the DCC claim is specifically the broadcast-master channel, not the episodes as known works.

channel_type: user-uploaded music/photo/video hosting corpus
discard_mechanism: server migration; MySpace stated older photos, videos, and audio became unavailable
inference_statement: INFERENCE: demos and early works with no independent copies are no longer publicly recoverable; but whether every item lacked an independent copy is unknown — many uploaders retained originals.
known_fact: Reports estimate 50+ million songs from ~14 million artists (uploads 2003-2015) became unavailable. MySpace's documented explanation is a server migration. Intentional-deletion speculation is NOT repeated here — it is unsupported.
name: MySpace server migration made 2003-2015 user uploads unavailable
notes: Soft penalty PLATFORM: much content was known to uploaders and many originals survive privately; the lost remainder is the public-corpus channel.

channel_type: free personal web hosting corpus (1995-2009)
discard_mechanism: Yahoo shut down GeoCities US on October 26, 2009; data not personally archived by owners declared irrecoverable
inference_statement: INFERENCE: uncrawled pages — those never visited by any rescue crawler — are gone without enumeration, since Yahoo released no directory. The crawled fraction is not the channel.
known_fact: The Internet Archive attempted to save as many of ~38 million pages as possible; the independent Archive Team rescued about a terabyte in a six-month crawl. Yahoo refused to release directory lists; crawls were incomplete and different rescue projects captured different fractions.
name: GeoCities shut down October 2009; ~38 million pages deleted
notes: Soft penalty PLATFORM: volunteer rescue captured a substantial-but-incomplete fraction; the uncrawled remainder is the DCC remainder.

channel_type: TOXicology Data NETwork: integrated toxicology/environmental-health database cluster + API + mobile apps
discard_mechanism: planned retirement; most databases migrated to PubChem/PubMed/Bookshelf; TOXNET API, mobile site, and LactMed apps retired; some databases retired outright
inference_statement: INFERENCE: retired databases and the Toxmap interface's query/visualization functionality constituted a channel (API access patterns, curated interface state) not fully enumerated by the migrated content.
known_fact: NLM Technical Bulletin: TOXNET retired Dec 16, 2019. Most content migrated to PubChem, PubMed, Bookshelf, or returned to source organizations (e.g., EPA). 'Some databases will be retired.' Toxmap — the pollution-mapping interface researchers relied on for visualization — was shuttered without a migration path (Popular Science, 2019).
name: NLM retired TOXNET December 16, 2019; Toxmap interface discontinued
notes: Soft penalty MIGRATION: most content demonstrably re-homed (fails G8 partially — elsewhere reconstructs much). The DCC remainder is the retired databases plus the Toxmap interface channel.

channel_type: 1,478-1,500 analog magnetic tapes + obsolete FR-900 drives (1966-1967 lunar imagery)
discard_mechanism: discard averted: tapes were headed for scrapping; obsolete drives had to be rebuilt to read them
inference_statement: CONTROL: discard averted, so no DCC claim is made. Logged to show the DCC loss shape (unreadable channel with unenumerated remainder) when retention wins.
known_fact: Most of ~1,500 tapes were recovered; project extracted detail absent from familiar reproductions. Parts of several images remained missing.
name: Lunar Orbiter tapes nearly scrapped; recovered by LOIRP (CONTROL)
notes: CONTROL. Discard was threatened, not completed; the recovered channel demonstrates what DCC loses.

channel_type: two LV-ROM interactive videodiscs + BBC Micro playback system (1986 survey of UK life)
discard_mechanism: discard averted: playback infrastructure died (Acorn BBC Micro + LV-ROM player); discs far outlived the system
inference_statement: CONTROL: playback-loss is a DCC discard mechanism, but the channel was rescued, so no DCC claim is made. Logged because it is the canonical infrastructure-loss case.
known_fact: The 1986 survey (a million contributors, ~150,000 pages of text, 20,000+ photos) became inaccessible by 2002. CAMiLEON (Leeds/Michigan) built an emulation of the obsolete BBC computer and videodisc player; later Domesday Reloaded put the data online.
name: BBC Domesday Project unreadable by 2002; rescued via CAMiLEON emulation (CONTROL)
notes: CONTROL. Demonstrates G3's playback-infrastructure clause and why the class tracks it as a discard mechanism.

channel_type: open-reel magnetic tapes of Apollo 15/17 subsurface temperature data, 1975-1977
discard_mechanism: discard averted by recovery: only 1971-1974 tapes were archived at NSSDC; 1975-1977 tapes never archived and presumed lost until tracked down in 2010
inference_statement: CONTROL: the channel was recovered, so no DCC claim is made. Logged because it shows the DCC remainder can be scientifically decisive — the recovered channel answered a question the retained archive could not.
known_fact: Nagihara's team recovered 440 tapes from 1975-1977 in 2010; the recovered data solved the decades-old mystery of the moon's post-deployment surface warming (astronaut-disturbed regolith darkening).
name: Apollo heat-flow experiment tapes lost then recovered 2010 (CONTROL)
notes: CONTROL. The strongest evidence that DCC's 'interrogation capacity' discriminator (G8) names something real.

channel_type: 1964-1978 Nimbus meteorological satellite magnetic tapes + 70mm film
discard_mechanism: discard averted: tapes boxed to government warehouses in Maryland/North Carolina; media past end of life; 'dark data' until the Nimbus Data Rescue Project
inference_statement: CONTROL: recovery succeeded, so no DCC claim is made. Logged as the canonical 'dark data' control: the channel existed and was unenumerated, but retention won.
known_fact: NSIDC's Nimbus data recovery project won the International Data Rescue Award in the Geosciences (2013): recovered, reprocessed, and digitized Nimbus I-III infrared/visible data, yielding the earliest satellite maps of Arctic and Antarctic sea ice, extending the sea-ice record 10-15 years.
name: Nimbus satellite tapes went 'dark' in warehouses; recovered by NSIDC/NASA (CONTROL)
notes: CONTROL. 'Dark data' (Gallaher: tapes languished in a government storage facility) is adjacent to DCC's unenumerated remainder but resolved by recovery.

channel_type: Landsat 1-7 downlink tapes held at International Cooperator ground stations
discard_mechanism: discard averted: no systematic transfer to USGS EROS; data degrading in 'less than pristine' storage; ~6.4M Landsat 4-7 + 486k Landsat 1-3 scenes repatriated since 2010
inference_statement: CONTROL: systematic recovery is succeeding, so no DCC claim is made. Logged because the pre-2010 state was the DCC shape: an unenumerated distributed channel at risk of discard.
known_fact: USGS: roughly two-thirds of Landsat data collected 1972-1999 remained largely untapped at ground stations; Landsat Global Archive Consolidation has repatriated millions of scenes since 2010 (5 millionth scene ingested April 2018).
name: Two-thirds of 1972-1999 Landsat data untapped at ground stations; repatriated via LGAC (CONTROL)
notes: CONTROL. Primary institutional source (USGS). Shows DCC's complement: the policy response to the same risk.

channel_type: the first web server at CERN (info.cern.ch, 1990-1993)
discard_mechanism: discard averted by duplicate: the original site was deleted; a 1992 copy survived on a line-mode-browser development machine and was used for the 2013 restoration
inference_statement: CONTROL: a complete duplicate survived, so G5 fails and no DCC claim is made. Logged as the G5 boundary case: duplicate survival defeats the class.
known_fact: CERN: the first website was deleted from its original server; in 2013 CERN restored it from a surviving 1992 copy of the code found on an old machine. The restored version is an approximation, not byte-identical.
name: First website deleted at CERN; restored from surviving 1992 copy (CONTROL)
notes: CONTROL. Source URL is CERN's birth-of-the-web page from search results — the restoration story is documented there. Flag: URL not re-verified in this session beyond the search snippet; honesty note in SESSION.md.

channel_type: n/a — meta-study of 516 morphology datasets, not a channel instance
discard_mechanism: n/a — measures the decay rate of researcher-stewarded channels (dead email addresses, obsolete storage)
inference_statement: META: supports DCC's motivation (individual stewardship is the dominant discard mechanism) but is not itself a channel instance. No DCC claim is made on it.
known_fact: Current Biology 24(1):94-97: for papers where authors gave data status, odds of a dataset being extant fell 17% per year of article age; working-author-email odds fell 7%/year. Only 121 of 516 datasets (23%) confirmed extant.
name: Vines et al. 2014: research data availability declines 17%/year (META)
notes: CONTROL/META. The decay-rate evidence behind the class's urgency claim. arXiv link is the preprint of the published paper.
